definition: An AI that produces new content (text, image, code) from a simple instruction, instead of executing a single programmed task.

definition: The basic unit an LLM reads and produces: a chunk of a word. The length of exchanges and their cost are measured in tokens.

definition: The instruction you give the AI. A good prompt — clear, with context and goal — changes everything about the result.
Capable of processing multiple types of input — text, image, audio — not just text.

definition: A model whose trained parameters can be downloaded and used under a license. Training data and code are not necessarily open.

definition: The American lab that creates Claude, focused on model reliability and safety.
Anthropic’s model family and assistant, used through conversation, Cowork, Claude Code or Claude Design.
Claude model families with different capability, speed and cost tradeoffs. The catalog also includes Fable; check versions before comparing.
Three ways to use Claude: chat (Chat), delegate office work (Cowork), act on files and projects (Code).
An interface for executing commands on a computer. Before running an AI-proposed command, understand which files or services it affects.
An interface for software to request data or actions from another service under defined rules and permissions.
An open protocol connecting AI applications to data and tools. It standardizes communication; permissions and integrations still need configuration.
A system using a model and tools to pursue a goal across multiple steps, within a defined scope and controls.
A platform for hosting Git repositories and collaborating on code. Tests and deployments can be automated when configured.
Files tracked with version history. A Git repository can be local or hosted on a platform such as GitHub.
A record of changes in Git history, with an identifier and message, helping explain, compare and retrieve project versions.
A timer that launches a task automatically at regular intervals (e.g. every morning at 7am).
A standard format for automatically pulling new articles from a site. The basic building block of any monitoring setup.
A program that posts messages on Telegram; a public channel is followable by anyone via a simple link.
A file Claude reads at startup: tone, conventions, pitfalls. It saves you from re-explaining everything every conversation.
A method that turns lessons learned into reusable instructions, tools or tests. Improvement depends on corrections actually being retained and applied.
Programming by describing your intent in plain language and letting AI generate the code. Term popularized by Andrej Karpathy.
The art of ranking well in search engines (Google…).
The SEO equivalent for AI: optimizing your content to be **cited** by assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity). That's the goal of this site.

definition: The organization behind GPT models, ChatGPT and Codex. Provider, application and model describe different layers.
OpenAI’s tool for conversation, research, analysis and creation with AI. Capabilities depend on the selected model, available tools and granted access.
A way to delegate work to ChatGPT through to a reviewable result: analysis, documents, presentations or research using authorized tools.
OpenAI’s agent for project work: understanding files, editing code, running tests and preparing reviewable results. It uses a GPT model.
A family of OpenAI models. GPT is the engine; ChatGPT and Codex provide interfaces and tools for using it.
An OpenAI model for complex reasoning, coding and research tasks. Distinct from Project Astra, Google DeepMind’s project.
GPT variants: Sol balances capability, speed and cost; Luna targets focused, fast tasks. Versions and access change over time.
Anthropic’s coding agent. It explores a project, edits files and uses tools to build, test or fix software.
Claude’s workspace for delegating work, including tasks involving files and documents, within the access authorized by the user.
Anthropic’s product for creating designs, prototypes, presentations and visual materials through conversation. Results can be refined and handed to Claude Code.
A Claude model family listed alongside Opus, Sonnet and Haiku in Anthropic’s catalog. This is a model name, not a design application.
Google’s AI research and development organization, behind Gemini models and the multimodal assistant research project Project Astra.
The name of Google’s model family and assistant application. Specify “Gemini model” or “Gemini app” to distinguish the two.
Google DeepMind’s research project exploring an assistant that understands voice, video and its surroundings. Some capabilities feed into Gemini Live.
The French company developing AI models and products including Mistral Vibe. Check each model’s license before calling it open source.
Mistral’s product combining a work assistant, formerly Le Chat, with a coding agent. An example of product naming evolving over time.
Google’s tool, formerly NotebookLM, for exploring sources, asking questions and producing summaries, including audio. Answers still need checking.
A search tool that synthesizes information and provides source links. Citations make answers checkable; they do not guarantee accuracy.
An AI development environment and coding agent for understanding projects, writing code, fixing errors and reviewing changes.
GitHub’s development assistant: code suggestions, chat, review assistance and agent capabilities depending on context. Distinct from other products named Copilot.
An AI audio and voice platform with speech synthesis, transcription and voice tools. It is used in the Podcast iA production process.
A platform for sharing and discovering models, datasets and demonstrations. Each resource has its own terms of use.
A tool for running models on your machine, with cloud options too. Memory requirements and permitted uses depend on the model.
A trained system that turns input into predictions or content. One application can combine multiple models and tools.
Learning patterns from data to perform a task without manually writing every decision rule.
The phase when model parameters are adjusted using data. Distinct from everyday use to produce responses.
Using an already trained model to produce an answer or prediction from new input.
The amount of information a model can process in one request: instructions, conversation, documents and response. A large window does not guarantee understanding.
Information saved and reused across interactions. Memory depends on the application and differs from current context and knowledge acquired during training.
Additional model work on a complex task. Higher effort can increase time and cost without ensuring a correct answer.
Retrieve information from documents, then provide it to a model to build an answer. Useful for internal knowledge without retraining.
A numerical representation of content used to compare semantic similarity, notably to retrieve relevant passages.
Storage and search for numerical content representations. A common component of semantic search and RAG systems.
Additional training on selected examples to adapt model behavior. Adding documents to a conversation is not fine-tuning.
Tests on representative cases that measure AI system quality, compare versions and detect regressions.
A set of tests used to compare systems. A strong score does not by itself establish quality for your own work.
Instructions defining the assistant’s role and behavior. They complement user requests within the product’s instruction hierarchy.
Including a few examples of the desired result in a prompt to clarify the format or task without retraining.
The model requests a function such as search, calculation or file reading. Host software executes an authorized action and returns its result.
An integration providing access to a service or its data within granted permissions. Reading and editing require different rights.
Reusable instructions, sometimes bundled with files and scripts, that teach an agent how to perform a particular task.
An extension bundling additional capabilities such as tools, connections or instructions. Contents and permissions depend on the host application.
An instruction file for agents working on a project: structure, commands, tests and conventions. Complements the human-facing README.
An agent delegated a subtask by another agent. Its scope must be defined and its results combined with the main work.
Organizing a workflow’s steps, tools and agents: who acts, in which order, using which data and checkpoints.
An agent’s ability to interact with an interface by reading screens, clicking and typing. Sensitive actions still need appropriate permissions and confirmation.
Misleading instructions in content an agent reads, intended to redirect its task. A page or document is data, not authorization.
Limits and controls around AI systems: restricted access, output checks and approvals before certain actions. No individual safeguard is infallible.
A person checks a result or approves an action before execution. The review should specify the action and data involved.
A response following a data schema rather than free text. Useful for software; valid formatting does not guarantee correct values.
Turning text into speech. Podcast quality also depends on writing, pacing, pronunciation and listening checks.
Turning recorded speech into text. Names, noise and multiple speakers can introduce errors requiring correction.
Extracting text from an image or scanned document. Recognizing characters and understanding a document’s meaning are different tasks.
Creating an image from instructions and, depending on the tool, reference images. Character consistency requires references and iterative corrections.
Editing a region of an image while preserving the rest as much as possible. A mask usually identifies the target area.
The android character created for Hugo’s AI watch: comic partner and podcast visual identity. An editorial character, not an AI model.
Shared visual rules and components: colors, typography, spacing and interface elements. They make designs consistent across formats.
A version used to test an idea or journey before full implementation. A convincing prototype is not necessarily a production-ready product.
Software licensed for use, study, modification and redistribution. Visible code, free access and open weights alone do not establish open-source status.
A line of work in Git history for preparing changes before integration.
An additional working directory linked to the same Git repository, useful for working on branches without mixing in-progress file changes.
A proposal of changes for review before integration, collecting diffs, discussion and available checks for a change.
A comparison of file or project versions showing additions, changes and deletions. A foundation for code review.
A subscription provides application access within limits. An API lets software call a service; permissions and billing may be separate.
A research mode that explores multiple sources and prepares a synthesis. Citations, dates and conclusions still need review.
Building an answer from identifiable documents or results. Keeping references helps distinguish retrieved facts from model inferences.
